subject: DSM in R: What are we doing wrong with dsm and plotting transects and segments?

messages.author: 512996ea4ff0ea65
messages.subject: DSM in R: What are we doing wrong with dsm and plotting transects and segments?
parts:
Hi everybdoy

We are starting to use dsm based in R because it look more flexible than the DISTANCE module, for example handling strip transects.

For learning how to use the dsm package in R we are using the "mexico-analysis" example provided by Miller and others.

We reached at the point of modelling and get results Ok (fitting a dsm). However we are stucked in an issue regarding the plotting of transects and segments. And I don´t know if this issue may affect analysis results.

The data comes from a helicopter survey of guanacos (a large herbivory) in Tierra del fuego. Data were get from georreferenced pictures taken from a helicopter, assuming a strip transect method of 700m width strip at each side.

I attach a figure of the area intended and the flight path segments (Guanacos DSM prueba). The path didn t follow a design based approach because of logistical constraints (money). That is why dsm sound good for us. You may see the shape of the flight path, doing a round clockwise from the south to the north  and back forth.

I also attach the R file as well as the data we are using. Positions fo sightings and segments were derived from geographic coordinates using the latlong2km code.

As you may see from the plots coming from R, the segments are drawn following a wierd pattern, like connecting points that must be apart in the flight order. I tried to solve this getting the data in the flight order and nothing changed.

Any help is appreciated

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] DSM in R: What are we doing wrong with dsm and plotting transects and segments?
parts:
Adrian:

Something has gone wrong with the formatting of x and y in your "segment.data" object that gets read from "2mar10seg.csv"  I've looked at the .csv file and I could not make sense of it to sort out the problem.  But if you issue "head(segment.data)" after reading it in, you will find that commas and decimal places have been swapped (because of current locale). 

           x          y  latitude longitude
1  -6.091,56 -25.135,39 -54.46393 -67.81759
2  -7.016,58 -24.086,04 -54.45450 -67.83187
3  -7.788,01 -22.927,28 -54.44408 -67.84378

This results in R interpreting numbers as factors and I predict that is why your ggplot looks bizarre.  See if the situation improves when you sort that out.

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] DSM in R: What are we doing wrong with dsm and plotting transects and segments?
parts:
Dear Eric,

Thanks for the fast reply....


I edited the csv files and nothing changed (well the plot vhanegd a little bit but looks the same)

I wonder if the shape of the flight path may affect the outcomes...I explain why...

Our flight path is not straight in terms of classical distance sampling. We flew along wide meadows delimited by forest patches, to avoid missing sightings due to the forest cover.

So some segments are not straight and are S shaped or "twisted".

I wonder how dsm instructs to plot a transect or segment, when the csv segment data only provides the central coordinate of the segment and the effort (location of the middle of segment and length of this segment), and the only clue that may help R or dsm to draw the transect would be the position of sightings, provided in other csv file (the distance data).
If I am right then dsm can only handle straight transects?

Other solution I imagine is to reduce the amount of transects or segments, if dsm has a limit on the amount of these than can handle....

Thanks again





have
